pairs.distinction: Gridlock is about problems in the world staying put; Unheard is about my own effort getting no response.
pairs.reason: Someone who has never spoken up can feel stuck problems, and someone who speaks up can feel unheard even on things that are moving.

pairs.distinction: Meetings is about the groups I'm in; Gridlock is about the place I live.
pairs.reason: A person stuck in a talk-only committee picks a different card than a person watching the same potholes for ten years.

pairs.distinction: Giving is about money and not knowing if it works; Unheard is about voice and getting no response.
pairs.reason: Doubting where a donation of money goes and feeling ignored after speaking up are different experiences with different fixes.

pairs.distinction: Allies is about not finding others who care; Unheard is about my effort going nowhere.
pairs.reason: One is about company and the other about results, so a person can tell at a glance which one is theirs.

pairs.distinction: Allies is about finding people who share a cause; Neighbors is about not knowing the people on my street at all.
pairs.reason: Someone can know every neighbor and still feel alone in caring about an issue, and the other way round.

pairs.distinction: Coordination is the practical search for existing efforts and groups; Allies is the feeling of being the only one who cares.
pairs.reason: They sit close, but the sharper Allies line (feeling alone) makes the choice easy against Coordination (can't find who's already working on it).

pairs.distinction: Coordination is about finding who is already working on a cause; Local news is about knowing what is going on in town.
pairs.reason: The Coordination wording has moved from its ID toward finding existing efforts, which is what keeps it apart from Local news.

pairs.distinction: Helping is not knowing what to do; Allies is not knowing who else cares.
pairs.reason: What to do and who to do it with are different gaps, and people usually know which one they have.

pairs.distinction: Helping is before acting; Unheard is after acting with nothing to show for it.
pairs.reason: A person who hasn't started and a person who tried and got nothing would not mistake one card for the other.

pairs.distinction: Helping is about time and action; Giving is about money and whether it works.
pairs.reason: Both start with 'I'd', but one is about doing and the other about paying, so they lead to different fixes.

pairs.distinction: Volunteers is the organizer's view of a thin bench; Helping is the would-be helper's view.
pairs.reason: They are two sides of the same gap, and each side would pick its own card.

pairs.distinction: Volunteers is about too few people carrying the work; Meetings is about groups that don't act.
pairs.reason: A group can get plenty done on the backs of three people, or have many members and still do nothing.

pairs.distinction: Collaborators is about having a specific idea and no one to build it with; Allies is about not finding others who care.
pairs.reason: Someone with a project in hand is looking for builders, not just company.

pairs.distinction: Collaborators is about a shared idea needing a team; Creativity on the personal page is about losing time to make things at all.
pairs.reason: One is about people to build with and the other about room in my own life to make things, so they are different pains, not one pain on two pages.
